answer: Propose a registry for ivory and opal artifacts. Each voting ID pays $10 per epoch and transcribes a distinct inventory page. A ledger binds each settled, nonrefundable payment and page to one ID. Two assigned auditors compare the transcript with its scan; both must approve before voting opens. Rejection or a missed deadline means no vote and no refund. A Sybil spiral of n IDs costs at least $10n per epoch; receipts cannot be reused. Registrar censorship, auditor collusion and wealthy operators remain threats.
